verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses at the Tent of Meeting in the Sinai wilderness. It was day one of month two, in the second year after Israel left Egypt.
“Take a census of the whole Israelite community. Go by clan and family, writing down the names of the men one by one.
You and Aaron will count every man in Israel who’s twenty or older and able to go to war. Count them by division.
One man from every tribe will help you. Each one must be the head of his family.
Here are the men who’ll stand with you. From Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur.
From Simeon: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
From Judah: Nahshon son of Amminadab.
From Issachar: Nethanel son of Zuar.
From Zebulun: Eliab son of Helon.
From Joseph’s descendants: Elishama son of Ammihud from Ephraim, and Gamaliel son of Pedahzur from Manasseh.
From Benjamin: Abidan son of Gideoni.
From Dan: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
From Asher: Pagiel son of Ochran.
From Gad: Eliasaph son of Deuel.
From Naphtali: Ahira son of Enan.”
These were the men called out from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes and the heads of Israel’s thousands.
Moses and Aaron brought together the men named on that list.
On day one of month two, they gathered the whole community. The men twenty and older registered by name, one by one, giving their ancestry by clan and family.
Moses counted them there in the Sinai wilderness, just as Yahweh had told him.
First were the descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn. They were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming each man twenty or older who could go to war.
Reuben’s tribe had 46,500 men on the list.
Simeon’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming each man twenty or older who could go to war.
Simeon’s tribe had 59,300 men on the list.
Gad’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Gad’s tribe had 45,650 men on the list.
Judah’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Judah’s tribe had 74,600 men on the list.
Issachar’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Issachar’s tribe had 54,400 men on the list.
Zebulun’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Zebulun’s tribe had 57,400 men on the list.
From Joseph’s descendants, Ephraim’s line was listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Ephraim’s tribe had 40,500 men on the list.
Manasseh’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Manasseh’s tribe had 32,200 men on the list.
Benjamin’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Benjamin’s tribe had 35,400 men on the list.
Dan’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Dan’s tribe had 62,700 men on the list.
Asher’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Asher’s tribe had 41,500 men on the list.
Naphtali’s descendants were listed by generation, clan, and family, naming the men twenty or older who could go to war.
Naphtali’s tribe had 53,400 men on the list.
That’s who Moses, Aaron, and the twelve leaders of Israel counted. Each leader represented his own ancestral family.
They counted Israel’s men by their ancestral families, everyone twenty or older who could go to war.
The total was 603,550.
The Levites weren’t counted with the others by ancestral tribe.
That’s because Yahweh had told Moses:
“Leave the tribe of Levi out of this count. Don’t register them with the rest of Israel.

Put the Levites in charge of the Tabernacle of the Testimony, its furnishings, and everything that belongs to it. They’ll carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, take care of it, and camp around it.
When the tabernacle needs to move, the Levites will take it down. When it needs to go back up, they’ll set it up. Any outsider who comes near must be put to death.
The Israelites will pitch their tents by division, each person in their own camp under their own banner.
But the Levites will camp around the Tabernacle of the Testimony so wrath doesn’t fall on the Israelite community. The Levites are responsible for taking care of the Tabernacle of the Testimony.”
The Israelites did exactly what Yahweh had told Moses.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“The Israelites will camp around the Tent of Meeting, leaving some space between the camps and the tent. Everyone will camp under their own standard, with their family banners.
“On the east, toward the sunrise, Judah’s divisions will camp under Judah’s standard. Nahshon son of Amminadab will lead Judah’s people.
His division had 74,600 men in the count.
“Issachar’s tribe will camp next to them. Nethanel son of Zuar will lead Issachar’s people.
His division had 54,400 men in the count.
“Then comes Zebulun’s tribe. Eliab son of Helon will lead Zebulun’s people.
His division had 57,400 men in the count.
“All the divisions in Judah’s camp came to 186,400. They’ll head out first.
“On the south, Reuben’s divisions will camp under Reuben’s standard. Elizur son of Shedeur will lead Reuben’s people.
His division had 46,500 men in the count.
“Simeon’s tribe will camp next to them. Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai will lead Simeon’s people.
His division had 59,300 men in the count.
“Then comes Gad’s tribe. Eliasaph son of Reuel will lead Gad’s people.
His division had 45,650 men in the count.
“All the fighting divisions in Reuben’s camp came to 151,450. They’ll head out second.
“Then the Tent of Meeting will move out with the Levites’ camp in the middle of the other camps. They’ll travel in the same order they camp, everyone in place under their own standard.
“On the west, Ephraim’s divisions will camp under Ephraim’s standard. Elishama son of Ammihud will lead Ephraim’s people.
His division had 40,500 men in the count.
“Manasseh’s tribe will camp next to them. Gamaliel son of Pedahzur will lead Manasseh’s people.
His division had 32,200 men in the count.
“Then comes Benjamin’s tribe. Abidan son of Gideoni will lead Benjamin’s people.
His fighting men came to 35,400 in the count.
“All the divisions in Ephraim’s camp came to 108,100. They’ll head out third.
“On the north, Dan’s divisions will camp under Dan’s standard. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai will lead Dan’s people.
His division had 62,700 men in the count.
“Asher’s tribe will camp next to them. Pagiel son of Ochran will lead Asher’s people.
His division had 41,500 men in the count.
“Then comes Naphtali’s tribe. Ahira son of Enan will lead Naphtali’s people.
His division had 53,400 men in the count.
“Dan’s camp came to 157,600 in all. They’ll head out last, each division under its own standard.”
That’s the count of the Israelites by ancestral family. All the fighting divisions across the camps came to 603,550.
The Levites weren’t included in Israel’s count, just as Yahweh had told Moses.
The Israelites did everything Yahweh told Moses. They camped under their standards and moved out under them, each person with their own clan and ancestral family.
Here’s the family record of Aaron and Moses from the time Yahweh spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
Aaron’s sons were Nadab, the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Those were Aaron’s sons, the priests who were anointed and set apart to serve as priests.
Nadab and Abihu died before Yahweh in the Sinai wilderness when they offered fire he hadn’t commanded. They left no children. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was there.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Bring the tribe of Levi forward and put them at the service of Aaron the priest.
They’ll carry out his duties and the duties of the whole community in front of the Tent of Meeting. They’ll do the work of the tabernacle.
They’ll look after all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting and handle the Israelites’ responsibilities for the work of the tabernacle.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They’re assigned to him completely on behalf of the Israelites.
Put Aaron and his sons in charge of their priestly duties. Any outsider who comes near must be put to death.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Look, I’ve taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among them. The Levites belong to me,
because all the firstborn are mine. The day I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart all Israel’s firstborn for myself, people and animals alike. They’re mine. I’m Yahweh.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses in the Sinai wilderness:
“Count Levi’s descendants by ancestral family and clan. Count every male a month old or older.”
Moses counted them as Yahweh had told him to do.
Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershon’s sons were Libni and Shimei, each with his own clan.
Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, each with his own clan.
Merari’s sons were Mahli and Mushi, each with his own clan. These were the Levite clans by ancestral family.
Gershon’s line included the Libnite and Shimeite clans. Those were the Gershonite clans.
The count of their males a month old or older came to 7,500.
The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
Eliasaph son of Lael was to lead the Gershonite ancestral family.
At the Tent of Meeting, Gershon’s descendants were responsible for the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, and the screen at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
They also looked after the courtyard hangings, the screen at the entrance to the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar, and all the cords needed for that work.
Kohath’s line included the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite, and Uzzielite clans. Those were the Kohathite clans.
The count of their males a month old or older came to 8,600. They were responsible for the sanctuary’s duties.
The Kohathite clans were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
Elizaphan son of Uzziel was to lead the Kohathite clans.
They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the utensils used in the sanctuary, the screen, and all the work that went with them.
Eleazar son of Aaron the priest was to lead the Levite leaders. He was to oversee the people responsible for the sanctuary.
Merari’s line included the Mahlite and Mushite clans. Those were Merari’s clans.
The count of their males a month old or older came to 6,200.
Zuriel son of Abihail led Merari’s clans. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
Merari’s descendants were assigned the tabernacle’s boards, crossbars, posts, bases, all its equipment, and all the work that went with them.
They were also responsible for the posts around the courtyard, their bases, their pegs, and their cords.

Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons were to camp out front on the east, in front of the Tent of Meeting, facing the sunrise. They were to carry out the sanctuary’s duties on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who comes near must be put to death.
At Yahweh’s command, Moses and Aaron counted the Levites by clan. The total for all the males a month old or older was 22,000.
Yahweh told Moses, “Count every firstborn male among the Israelites who’s a month old or older, and record the number of names.
Take the Levites for me in place of all the Israelite firstborn. I’m Yahweh. Take the Levites’ livestock in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites’ livestock.”
Moses counted all the Israelite firstborn, just as Yahweh had told him.
The count by name of the firstborn males a month old or older came to 22,273.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Take the Levites in place of all the Israelite firstborn, and the Levites’ livestock in place of theirs. The Levites belong to me. I’m Yahweh.
There are 273 more Israelite firstborn than Levites. To redeem those extra firstborn,
collect five shekels per person, using the sanctuary shekel. A shekel is twenty gerahs.
Give that money to Aaron and his sons. It’s the price for redeeming the ones left over.”
Moses collected the redemption money from those beyond the number redeemed by the Levites.
From the Israelite firstborn he collected 1,365 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
Moses handed the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, just as Yahweh had told him.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Count Kohath’s descendants among the Levites by clan and ancestral family.
Count everyone from thirty to fifty years old who comes to serve and do the work at the Tent of Meeting.
“Here’s the work Kohath’s descendants will do at the Tent of Meeting. They’ll handle the most holy things.
When the camp moves out, Aaron and his sons will go in, take down the screening curtain, and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
They’ll put a sealskin cover over it, spread a blue cloth on top, and slide the carrying poles into place.
“Spread a blue cloth over the table for the sacred bread. Put the dishes, spoons, bowls, and cups for pouring on it. Keep the regular offering of bread on the table too.
Spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover it with sealskin, and slide the carrying poles into place.
“Take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand, its lamps, its wick trimmers, its trays for the trimmings, and all the oil containers used to tend the lamps.
Wrap the lampstand and all its utensils in sealskin and set the bundle on the carrying frame.
“Spread a blue cloth over the gold altar, cover it with sealskin, and slide the carrying poles into place.
“Take all the utensils used to serve in the sanctuary, wrap them in a blue cloth, cover them with sealskin, and put them on the carrying frame.
“Clear the ashes off the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
Put all the tools used at the altar on top: the fire pans, meat hooks, shovels, and basins. Spread a sealskin cover over the whole lot and slide the carrying poles into place.

“When the camp is ready to move and Aaron and his sons have covered the sanctuary and everything in it, Kohath’s descendants will come carry the covered items. They must keep their hands off the holy things themselves, or they’ll die. These are the things they’ll carry for the Tent of Meeting.

“Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will be in charge of the lamp oil, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He’ll oversee the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the sanctuary and its furnishings.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Don’t let the Kohathite clans be cut off from the Levites.
Do this so they’ll live when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons must go in first and assign each person their job and what to carry.
The Kohathites must never go in to look at the sanctuary, even for a moment, or they’ll die.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Count Gershon’s descendants too, by ancestral family and clan.
Count everyone from thirty to fifty years old who comes to serve and do the work at the Tent of Meeting.
“Here are the Gershonite clans’ jobs, including what they’ll carry:
the tabernacle curtains and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, the sealskin cover over it, and the screen at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

They’ll carry the courtyard hangings, the screen at the gate of the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar, their cords, and all the equipment that goes with them. They’ll do whatever work those things require.
Aaron and his sons will direct all the Gershonites’ work, including everything they carry and every job they do. Assign them responsibility for each load.
That’s the work of Gershon’s clans at the Tent of Meeting. Ithamar son of Aaron the priest will supervise them.
“Count Merari’s descendants by clan and ancestral family.
Count everyone from thirty to fifty years old who comes to serve and do the work at the Tent of Meeting.
Here’s what they’re responsible for carrying as part of their work at the Tent of Meeting: the tabernacle’s boards, crossbars, posts, and bases,
along with the posts around the courtyard, their bases, pegs, and cords, and all the equipment and work that go with them. List each item by name and assign it to someone to carry.
That’s the work of Merari’s clans at the Tent of Meeting. Ithamar son of Aaron the priest will supervise them.”
Moses, Aaron, and the community leaders counted the Kohathites by clan and ancestral family.
They counted everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve at the Tent of Meeting.
The count by clan came to 2,750.
That was the count of the Kohathite clans serving at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as Yahweh had commanded through Moses.
Gershon’s descendants were counted by clan and ancestral family.
The count covered everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve at the Tent of Meeting.
Their count by clan and ancestral family came to 2,630.
That was the count of Gershon’s clans serving at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as Yahweh had commanded.
The clans descended from Merari were counted by clan and ancestral family.
The count covered everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve at the Tent of Meeting.
Their count by clan came to 3,200.
That was the count of Merari’s clans. Moses and Aaron counted them as Yahweh had commanded through Moses.
Moses, Aaron, and Israel’s leaders counted the Levites by clan and ancestral family.
They counted everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to work at the Tent of Meeting, whether serving there or carrying the loads.
The total came to 8,580.
At Yahweh’s command, Moses counted them, assigning each person the work they would do and the load they would carry. He counted them just as Yahweh had told him.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites to send anyone with leprosy, anyone with a discharge, and anyone made unclean by a dead body out of the camp.
Send them outside the camp, men and women alike, so they don’t make the camp unclean. I live right there among you.”
The Israelites did what Yahweh had told Moses and sent those people outside the camp.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When a man or woman commits any of the wrongs people commit and is guilty of being unfaithful to Yahweh,
they must admit what they did and pay the person they wronged back in full, plus a fifth.
If there’s no relative to receive repayment, the repayment goes to Yahweh for the priest to keep, in addition to the ram used to make atonement for the person who did wrong.
Every holy gift the Israelites lift up as an offering and bring to the priest belongs to him.
Each person’s holy gifts are theirs to give. Whatever they give to the priest belongs to him.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Suppose a man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him.
Another man sleeps with her and she becomes unclean, but her husband doesn’t see it. Nobody else sees it either, and nobody catches her in the act.
Or suppose jealousy comes over her husband and he suspects his wife, whether she’s become unclean or she hasn’t.

He’ll bring his wife to the priest and bring an offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley meal. Don’t pour oil on it or add frankincense. It’s a grain offering for jealousy, a reminder that brings wrongdoing to mind.
The priest will bring her forward and have her stand before Yahweh.
He’ll take holy water in a clay pot and put some dust from the floor of the tabernacle into it.

The priest will have the woman stand before Yahweh, let her hair hang loose, and put the grain offering that serves as a reminder in her hands. It’s the offering for jealousy. The priest will hold the bitter water that brings a curse.

The priest will put her under oath and say, “If no other man has slept with you, and you haven’t gone astray and made yourself unclean while under your husband’s authority, may you be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
But if you’ve gone astray while under your husband’s authority and become unclean because another man has slept with you,”
the priest will put the woman under an oath that carries a curse and say, “May Yahweh make you a curse and an oath among your people when he makes your thigh waste away and your body swell.
May this water that brings a curse go into your belly, make your body swell, and make your thigh waste away.” The woman will answer, “Amen, amen.”
“‘The priest will write these curses in a book and wipe them into the bitter water.
He’ll have the woman drink the bitter water that brings the curse. The water will go into her and turn bitter.
The priest will take the grain offering for jealousy from the woman’s hand, wave it before Yahweh, and bring it to the altar.
He’ll take a handful as the portion that serves as a reminder and burn it on the altar. After that he’ll have the woman drink the water.

When she drinks it, if she’s become unclean and been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will go into her and turn bitter. Her body will swell, her thigh will waste away, and she’ll become a curse among her people.
If she hasn’t become unclean and is clean, she’ll be free of the curse and will conceive children.
“‘That’s the rule for jealousy when a wife goes astray and becomes unclean while under her husband’s authority,
or when jealousy takes hold of a man and he suspects his wife. He’ll have her stand before Yahweh, and the priest will carry out this whole rule with her.
The man will be free of guilt, and the woman will answer for her own wrongdoing.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘A man or woman can make a special vow as a Nazirite to set themselves apart for Yahweh.
They’ll stay away from wine and strong drink. That means no vinegar made from wine or other fermented drink, no grape juice, and no fresh grapes or raisins.
For the whole time they’re set apart, they won’t eat anything from the grapevine, right down to the seeds and skins.
“‘While the vow is in effect, no razor may touch their head. Until their time set apart for Yahweh is up, they’re holy and must let their hair grow long.
“‘For the whole time they’re set apart for Yahweh, they must stay away from dead bodies.
Even if their father, mother, brother, or sister dies, they must not make themselves unclean for them. The sign that they’re set apart for God is on their head.
They’re holy to Yahweh the whole time they’re set apart.
“‘If someone suddenly dies beside them and makes their consecrated head unclean, they must shave their head on the day they’re cleansed. They’ll shave it on day seven.
On day eight they’ll bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will offer one for sin and the other as a burnt offering. He’ll make atonement for them because of the sin involving the dead body and set their head apart as holy again that very day.
They’ll start their time set apart for Yahweh over and bring a year-old male lamb for a guilt offering. The days that already passed don’t count, because their time of separation was defiled.
“‘Here’s the rule for a Nazirite. When the time they vowed to be set apart is up, bring them to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
They’ll bring Yahweh a year-old male lamb with no defects for a burnt offering, a year-old female lamb with no defects for a sin offering, and a ram with no defects for a peace offering.
They’ll also bring a basket of bread made without yeast, with cakes of fine flour mixed with oil and thin unleavened wafers brushed with oil, along with the grain and drink offerings.
The priest will present these before Yahweh and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He’ll give Yahweh the ram as a peace offering, along with the basket of bread made without yeast. He’ll also make the accompanying grain and drink offerings.
At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting the Nazirite will shave off the hair from their time of separation and put it on the fire under the peace offering.
Once the Nazirite has shaved their head, the priest will take the boiled shoulder of the ram, a cake from the basket, and an unleavened wafer, and place them in the Nazirite’s hands.

The priest will wave them before Yahweh as a wave offering. Those portions are holy and belong to the priest, along with the breast that’s waved and the thigh that’s offered. After that the Nazirite can drink wine.

“‘That’s the rule for a Nazirite who makes a vow and brings an offering to Yahweh for being set apart, besides anything else they can afford to give. They must keep the vow they made according to the rules for their time of separation.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron and his sons, ‘Here’s how to bless the Israelites.’ Say to them:
‘May Yahweh bless you and keep you safe.
May Yahweh’s face shine on you, and may he show you grace.
May Yahweh turn his face toward you and give you peace.’
“That’s how they’ll put my name on the Israelites, and I’ll bless them.”
On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and set it apart as holy, along with all its furnishings. He also anointed the altar and all its tools and set them apart as holy.
Then Israel’s leaders brought their offerings. They were the heads of the ancestral families, the tribal leaders who had overseen the count.
They brought six covered wagons and twelve oxen before Yahweh. Every two leaders provided a wagon, and each leader provided an ox. They brought them to the front of the tabernacle.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Accept these gifts. Use them for the work of the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the Levites according to the work each one does.”
Moses took the wagons and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave Gershon’s descendants two wagons and four oxen for the work they did.
He gave Merari’s descendants four wagons and eight oxen for their work under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
He gave Kohath’s descendants none. Their job was to handle the holy things of the sanctuary, and they carried those on their shoulders.
On the day the altar was anointed, the leaders brought their gifts for its dedication and presented them in front of the altar.
Yahweh told Moses, “Have each leader bring his gift on his own day to dedicate the altar.”
Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah, brought his offering on the first day.
His offering was: one silver platter weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold ladle weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For a burnt offering, he brought one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb.
For a sin offering, he brought one male goat.
For the peace offerings, he brought two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was Nahshon son of Amminadab’s offering.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his offering.
His offering was: one silver platter weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold ladle weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For a burnt offering, he brought one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb.
For a sin offering, he brought one male goat.
For the peace offerings, he brought two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was Nethanel son of Zuar’s offering.
On the third day, Eliab son of Helon, the leader of Zebulun,

brought this offering: one silver platter weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold ladle weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For a burnt offering, he brought one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb.
For a sin offering, he brought one male goat.
For the peace offerings, he brought two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was Eliab son of Helon’s offering.
On the fourth day, Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of Reuben,

brought this offering: one silver platter weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold ladle weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For a burnt offering, he brought one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb.
For a sin offering, he brought one male goat.
For the peace offerings, he brought two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was Elizur son of Shedeur’s offering.
On the fifth day, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of Simeon,

brought this offering: one silver platter weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold ladle weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For a burnt offering, he brought one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb.
For a sin offering, he brought one male goat.
For the peace offerings, he brought two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai’s offering.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph son of Deuel, the leader of Gad,

brought this offering: one silver platter weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold ladle weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For a burnt offering, he brought one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb.
For a sin offering, he brought one male goat.

Here’s what Israel’s leaders brought to dedicate the altar on the day it was anointed: twelve silver platters, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold ladles.
Each silver platter weighed 130 shekels and each bowl weighed 70. All the silver vessels together weighed 2,400 shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
The twelve gold ladles, full of incense, each weighed 10 shekels by the sanctuary measure. Together they weighed 120 shekels of gold.
The burnt offerings totaled twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve year-old male lambs, with their grain offerings. There were also twelve male goats for a sin offering.
The peace offerings totaled twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty year-old male lambs. Those were the gifts for dedicating the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with Yahweh, he heard Yahweh’s voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim, above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony. That’s where Yahweh spoke to him.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Aaron, ‘When you light the lamps, set all seven so they shine in front of the lampstand.’”
Aaron did exactly that. He lit the lamps to shine in front of the lampstand, just as Yahweh had told Moses.
The lampstand was made of hammered gold. It was hammered into shape from its base right up to its flowers. It was made to match the pattern Yahweh had shown Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them clean.
Here’s how: sprinkle them with the water for cleansing. Have them shave their whole bodies with a razor, wash their clothes, and make themselves clean.
Then have them bring a young bull and its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. Take another young bull for a sin offering.
Bring the Levites in front of the Tent of Meeting and call the whole Israelite community together.
Present the Levites before Yahweh. The Israelites will lay their hands on them.
Aaron will present the Levites before Yahweh as a wave offering on behalf of the Israelites, so they can do Yahweh’s work.
“Have the Levites lay their hands on the bulls’ heads. Offer one to Yahweh as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for the Levites.
Have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and present them to Yahweh as a wave offering.
That’s how you’ll set the Levites apart from the rest of Israel. They’ll belong to me.
“After that the Levites can go in to work at the Tent of Meeting. You’ll cleanse them and present them as a wave offering.
They’re given completely to me from among the Israelites. I’ve taken them in place of everyone who opens the womb, every firstborn in Israel.
All the firstborn in Israel belong to me, human and animal alike. On the day I struck down every firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart as holy for myself.
I’ve taken the Levites in place of all the Israelite firstborn.

From among the Israelites, I’ve given the Levites to Aaron and his sons as a gift. They’ll do Israel’s work at the Tent of Meeting and make atonement for the Israelites so no plague strikes them when they come near the sanctuary.”
Moses, Aaron, and the whole Israelite community did everything Yahweh had told Moses to do with the Levites.
The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes. Aaron presented them before Yahweh as a wave offering and made atonement for them to cleanse them.
After that, the Levites went in to work at the Tent of Meeting under Aaron and his sons. Everything was done for the Levites just as Yahweh had told Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Here’s what’s assigned to the Levites. From age twenty-five onward, they’ll come in to serve and do the work at the Tent of Meeting.
When they reach fifty, they’ll retire from doing that work and stop serving in that role.
They can help their fellow Levites carry out their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they won’t do the regular work themselves. That’s how you’ll assign the Levites their duties.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses in the Sinai wilderness in the first month of the second year after the Israelites left Egypt.
“Have the Israelites keep Passover at its appointed time.
Keep it on the evening of the fourteenth day of this month, right at the appointed time. Follow all its rules and instructions.”
So Moses told the Israelites to keep Passover.
They kept Passover in the Sinai wilderness on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month. They did everything Yahweh had told Moses.
Some men had become unclean because of a dead body, so they couldn’t keep Passover that day. They went to Moses and Aaron that very day.
They said to Moses, “We’re unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be left out when the rest of Israel brings Yahweh’s offering at the appointed time?”
Moses answered, “Wait here while I hear what Yahweh tells me about your situation.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘If anyone among you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body or away on a long trip, they must still keep Passover for Yahweh.
They’ll keep it on the evening of the fourteenth day of the second month. They’ll eat it with bread made without yeast and with bitter herbs.
They must leave none of it till morning or break any of its bones. They’ll keep it according to every Passover rule.

If someone is clean, isn’t away on a trip, and skips Passover, that person will be cut off from their people. They didn’t bring Yahweh’s offering at the appointed time, and they’ll answer for that sin.
“‘If a foreigner living among you wants to keep Passover for Yahweh, they must follow the Passover rules and instructions. The same rule applies to the foreigner and to anyone born in the land.’”
On the day the tabernacle went up, the cloud covered it, the Tent of the Testimony. From evening till morning, what hung over the tabernacle looked like fire. 🔥
That’s how it stayed: the cloud covered it, and at night it looked like fire.
Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, the Israelites moved on. Wherever the cloud settled, they set up camp.
At Yahweh’s command they moved on, and at Yahweh’s command they set up camp. As long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they stayed in camp.
When the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites followed Yahweh’s command and stayed put.
Sometimes the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for only a few days. At Yahweh’s command they stayed in camp, and at his command they moved on.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening till morning. When it lifted in the morning, they moved on. Day or night, whenever it lifted, they moved on.
Whether the cloud stayed over the tabernacle two days, a month, or a year, the Israelites stayed in camp without moving on. When it lifted, they moved on.
At Yahweh’s command they made camp, and at his command they moved on. They followed the instructions Yahweh gave them through Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call the community together and to signal when the camps should move out. 🎺
When both trumpets sound, the whole community will gather in front of you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
When only one sounds, the leaders who head Israel’s thousands will gather in front of you.
When you sound the alarm, the camps on the east side will move out.
Sound it a second time, and the camps on the south side will move out. Use the alarm to signal that it’s time to travel.
When you’re calling the assembly together, blow the trumpets without sounding the alarm.
“Aaron’s sons, the priests, will blow the trumpets. That rule stands for every generation.
When you go into battle in your own land against an enemy who’s oppressing you, sound the alarm with the trumpets. Yahweh your God will remember you and save you from your enemies.

“On your days of celebration, at your appointed festivals, and at the start of each month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. They’ll serve as a reminder for you before your God. I’m Yahweh your God.”
In the second year, on day twenty of the second month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the covenant.
The Israelites moved out from the Sinai wilderness in stages, and the cloud came to rest in the wilderness of Paran.
That was the first time they moved out at Yahweh’s command through Moses.
Judah’s camp moved out first under its standard, division by division. Nahshon son of Amminadab led Judah’s fighting men.
Nethanel son of Zuar led the fighting men from Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon led the fighting men from Zebulun.
The tabernacle was taken down, and Gershon’s and Merari’s descendants moved out carrying it.
Next came Reuben’s camp, marching under its standard, division by division. Elizur son of Shedeur led Reuben’s fighting men.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai led the fighting men from Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Deuel led the fighting men from Gad.
The Kohathites moved out carrying the holy things. The others set up the tabernacle before they arrived.
Ephraim’s camp moved out under its standard, division by division. Elishama son of Ammihud led Ephraim’s fighting men.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur led the fighting men from Manasseh.
Abidan son of Gideoni led the fighting men from Benjamin.
Dan’s camp moved out under its standard, division by division, guarding the rear of all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai led Dan’s fighting men.
Pagiel son of Ochran led the fighting men from Asher.
Ahira son of Enan led the fighting men from Naphtali.
That’s the order the Israelites traveled in, division by division, when they moved out.

Moses told Hobab, son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We’re headed to the place Yahweh said he’d give us. Come with us and we’ll treat you well, because Yahweh has promised good things for Israel.”
Hobab replied, “I’m going back to my own land and my own family. I’m not coming with you.”
Moses said, “Please don’t leave us. You know where we can camp out in the wilderness. You can be our eyes out there.
Come with us, and whatever good Yahweh does for us, we’ll do the same for you.”
They traveled three days from Yahweh’s mountain. The ark of Yahweh’s covenant went ahead of them on that three-day journey to find a place for them to rest.
Yahweh’s cloud was over them by day as they moved out from camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, Yahweh! Scatter your enemies! Let those who hate you run from you!”
And whenever it came to rest, he would say, “Come back, Yahweh, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
The people complained where Yahweh could hear them. When he heard, his anger flared up, and fire from Yahweh burned among them and tore through part of the edge of camp.
The people cried out to Moses. He prayed to Yahweh, and the fire died down.
They called that place Taberah because Yahweh’s fire burned among them there.
The mixed crowd traveling with them got intense cravings. The Israelites started crying again too. “Who’s going to give us some meat to eat?
Remember the fish we ate for free in Egypt? And the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic?
Now we don’t even feel like eating. Everywhere we look, it’s manna and more manna.”
The manna was like coriander seed and looked like bdellium resin.
People walked around collecting it, then ground it in mills or pounded it in mortars. They boiled it in pots and made cakes with it. It tasted like fresh oil.
When dew settled on the camp at night, the manna came down on it.
Moses heard families crying at the entrances to their tents. Yahweh was furious, and Moses was upset too.
Moses said to Yahweh, “Why have you treated your servant like this? How did I fall so far out of your favor that you put this whole crowd on my shoulders?
Did I conceive all these people? Did I give birth to them? Why tell me, ‘Carry them close like a nurse carries a nursing baby, all the way to the land you promised their ancestors’?
Where am I supposed to get meat for all these people? They’re crying right in front of me, saying, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
I can’t carry all these people on my own. It’s too heavy for me.
If this is how you’re going to treat me, then please, if I still have your favor, kill me now. Don’t make me live to see how miserable I’ve become.”
Yahweh told Moses, “Gather seventy of Israel’s elders for me, men you know to be elders and officers over the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.
I’ll come down and talk with you there. I’ll take some of the Spirit that’s on you and put it on them. They’ll carry the weight of the people with you so you don’t have to do it alone.

“Tell the people, ‘Set yourselves apart for tomorrow. You’re going to eat meat. Yahweh heard you crying, “Who’ll give us meat to eat? We had it good in Egypt.” So Yahweh will give you meat, and you’ll eat it.
You’ll be eating it for longer than one day, two days, five days, ten days, or even twenty days.
It’ll be a whole month, until it comes out your nose and makes you sick to think about it. You rejected Yahweh, who’s right here among you, and cried in front of him, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?”’”
Moses said, “I’m here among six hundred thousand men on foot, and you’ve said, ‘I’ll give them meat for a whole month.’
Would slaughtering the flocks and herds even be enough? Would rounding up all the fish in the sea be enough for them?”
Yahweh told Moses, “Has Yahweh’s hand gotten too short? You’ll see whether what I said happens to you.”
Moses went out and told the people what Yahweh had said. Then he gathered seventy elders and had them stand around the tent.

Yahweh came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they didn’t do it again.
Two men had stayed behind in camp. One was Eldad and the other was Medad. They were on the list but hadn’t gone out to the tent. The Spirit rested on them, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran to Moses and said, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in camp!”
Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant and one of his chosen men, said, “My lord Moses, stop them!”
Moses said, “Are you jealous for me? I wish all Yahweh’s people were prophets and that Yahweh would put his Spirit on every one of them!”
Moses and Israel’s elders went back into camp.
Yahweh sent a wind that brought quail in from the sea. The birds came down all around the camp, about a day’s walk in either direction and about two cubits above the ground.
The people gathered quail all that day, all night, and all the next day. The person who gathered the least still got ten homers. They spread the birds out all around the camp.
The meat was still between their teeth, before they’d even chewed it, when Yahweh’s anger flared against them. He struck them with a severe plague.
They called that place Kibroth Hattaavah because that’s where they buried the people who gave in to the craving.
From Kibroth Hattaavah they traveled to Hazeroth and stayed there.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because he’d married a Cushite woman. That was the woman he’d taken as his wife.
They said, “Is Moses the only one Yahweh has spoken through? Hasn’t he spoken through us too?” Yahweh heard them.
Moses was very humble, more humble than anyone else on earth.
Out of nowhere Yahweh told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “All three of you, out to the Tent of Meeting!” So the three of them went out.
Yahweh came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance to the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and they both stepped forward.
He said, “Listen to what I’m telling you. If there’s a prophet among you, I, Yahweh, make myself known in a vision and speak to that prophet in a dream.
Things are different with my servant Moses. He’s faithful throughout my household.
I speak to him directly, mouth to mouth. I speak plainly and without riddles, and he sees Yahweh’s form. So how were you able to speak against my servant Moses without being afraid?”
Yahweh’s anger flared against them, and he left.
When the cloud lifted from the tent, there was Miriam with leprosy, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw the leprosy.
Aaron told Moses, “Please, my lord, don’t hold this sin against us. We acted like fools and sinned.
Please don’t let her end up like a stillborn baby whose flesh is half gone when it comes out of its mother’s womb.”
Moses cried out to Yahweh, “God, please heal her. I’m begging you!”
Yahweh told Moses, “If her father had spit in her face, wouldn’t she carry that shame for seven days? Keep her outside the camp for seven days, and then bring her back in.”
Miriam was kept outside the camp for seven days. The people stayed put until she was brought back in.
After that, the people moved on from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Send men to scout Canaan, the land I’m giving the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each one a leader among his people.”
Moses sent them from the Paran wilderness as Yahweh commanded. Every one of them was a leader in Israel.
Here are their names. From Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur.
From Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori.
From Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From Issachar: Igal son of Joseph.
From Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun.
From Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu.
From Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi.
From Joseph’s line, through Manasseh: Gaddi son of Susi.
From Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli.
From Asher: Sethur son of Michael.
From Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi.
From Gad: Geuel son of Machi.
Those were the men Moses sent to scout the land. Moses called Hoshea son of Nun by the name Joshua.
Moses sent them to scout Canaan and told them, “Go up through the South and head into the hill country.
Check what the land is like and who lives there. Are the people strong or weak? Are there a few of them or a lot?
Is the land where they live good or bad? What are their towns like? Do they live in open camps or behind defenses?
Is the soil fertile or poor? Are there trees? Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit from the land.” It was the season when the first grapes ripened.
So they went up and scouted the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, at the entrance to Hamath.
They went up through the South and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They reached the valley of Eshcol and cut a branch with a single bunch of grapes. It took two of them to carry it on a pole between them. 🍇 They also brought some pomegranates and figs.
They called that place the valley of Eshcol because of the bunch of grapes the Israelites cut there.
After forty days of scouting the land, they came back.
They returned to Moses, Aaron, and the whole Israelite community at Kadesh in the Paran wilderness. They gave their report to everyone and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told Moses, “We went to the land you sent us to. It really does flow with milk and honey. Look, here’s some of its fruit.
But the people living there are strong, and the cities are huge and fortified. We even saw Anak’s descendants there.
Amalek lives in the South. The Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
Caleb quieted the people in front of Moses and said, “Let’s go up right now and take the land. We can do this!”
But the men who’d gone up with him said, “We can’t go up against those people. They’re stronger than we are.”
They spread a bad report among the Israelites about the land they’d scouted. “The land we explored eats up the people who live in it. Everyone we saw there was huge.
We saw the Nephilim there, Anak’s descendants who come from the Nephilim. We looked like grasshoppers to ourselves, and that’s how we looked to them too.”
The whole community raised their voices and cried. The people wept that night.
The Israelites complained against Moses and Aaron. The whole community said, “If only we’d died in Egypt or out here in this wilderness!
Why is Yahweh bringing us into that land to die by the sword? Our wives and little ones will be captured or killed! Wouldn’t we be better off going back to Egypt?”
They told each other, “Let’s pick a leader and go back to Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron fell facedown in front of the whole Israelite assembly.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of the men who’d scouted the land, tore their clothes.
They told the whole community, “The land we crossed and scouted is really, really good.
If Yahweh is pleased with us, he’ll bring us into that land and give it to us. It’s a land flowing with milk and honey.
Just don’t turn against Yahweh or be afraid of the people there. We’ll eat them up like bread. Their protection is gone, and Yahweh is with us. Don’t be scared of them.”
The whole community threatened to stone them. Then Yahweh’s glory appeared in the Tent of Meeting where all the Israelites could see it.
Yahweh said to Moses, “How long will these people despise me? How long will they refuse to trust me after all the signs I’ve done among them?
I’ll hit them with a plague and take away their inheritance. I’ll make you into a nation bigger and stronger than they are.”
Moses told Yahweh, “Then Egypt will hear about it. You brought these people out from among the Egyptians by your power.

The Egyptians will tell the people who live in this land. They’ve heard, Yahweh, that you’re among these people. They see you face to face, your cloud stands over them, and you go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you kill all these people at once, the nations that have heard about you will say,
‘Yahweh couldn’t get them into the land he promised them, so he killed them in the wilderness.’
Please show how great your power is, Lord, just as you said:

‘Yahweh is slow to get angry, full of faithful love, and forgives wrongdoing and rebellion. He never lets the guilty off the hook and brings the consequences of the parents’ wrongdoing on their children to the third and fourth generation.’
Please forgive these people for what they’ve done, because your faithful love is so great. You’ve forgiven them all the way from Egypt to now.”
Yahweh answered, “I’ve forgiven them, just as you asked.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth will be filled with Yahweh’s glory,
all those people saw my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the wilderness. They still put me to the test these ten times and refused to listen to me.
They won’t see the land I promised their ancestors. None of those who despised me will see it.
My servant Caleb had a different spirit and followed me with his whole heart. I’ll bring him into the land he went to, and his descendants will own it.
Since the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valley, turn around tomorrow and head into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”
Yahweh told Moses and Aaron:
“How long do I have to put up with this wicked crowd complaining about me? I’ve heard the Israelites grumbling against me.
Tell them, ‘As surely as I live, says Yahweh, I’ll do to you exactly what you said where I could hear you.
Your bodies will fall in this wilderness. Every one of you counted in the census, twenty years old or older, who complained against me,
will miss out on the land I swore I’d settle you in. Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun will be the only exceptions.
You said your little ones would be captured or killed. I’ll bring them in, and they’ll get to know the land you rejected.
As for you, your bodies will fall here in the wilderness.
Your children will wander in the wilderness for forty years and carry the cost of your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies is gone from the wilderness.
You scouted the land for forty days. For every day, you’ll carry the consequences of your wrongdoing for a year. That’s forty years, and you’ll know what it means to have me turn away from you.’
I, Yahweh, have spoken. I’ll do this to the whole wicked community that’s gathered against me. Here in this wilderness they’ll come to an end and die.”
The men Moses had sent to scout the land came back with a bad report that made the whole community complain against him.
Those men who brought the bad report died in a plague before Yahweh.
Out of the men who went to scout the land, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh stayed alive.
Moses told all the Israelites what Yahweh had said, and the people grieved deeply.
They got up early the next morning and climbed toward the top of the mountain. “Here we are,” they said. “We’ll go up to the place Yahweh promised. We know we sinned.”
Moses said, “Why are you going against Yahweh’s command now? This won’t work.
Stay down. Yahweh isn’t among you. If you go up, your enemies will strike you down.
The Amalekites and Canaanites are up there. You’ll fall by the sword because you turned away from Yahweh. He won’t be with you.”
But they went up toward the top of the mountain anyway, even though the ark of Yahweh’s covenant and Moses stayed in the camp.
The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in those hills came down, struck them, and drove them back as far as Hormah.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you get to the land I’m giving you to live in,

and bring Yahweh an offering through fire from your herd or flock, whether it’s a burnt offering or a sacrifice for a vow, a gift you give freely, or an offering at one of your festivals to make a pleasing smell for Yahweh,
the person bringing the offering must also give Yahweh a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
With each lamb, whether for a burnt offering or another sacrifice, bring a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
“‘For a ram, make a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil.
Bring a third of a hin of wine for the drink offering, for a smell that pleases Yahweh.
When you bring a bull to Yahweh as a burnt offering, as a sacrifice to keep a vow, or as a peace offering,
bring a grain offering with it: three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil.
Bring half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It’s an offering given through fire, with a smell that pleases Yahweh.
Do this for each bull, each ram, each male lamb, and each young goat.
However many animals you prepare, bring the required amounts for every one of them.
“‘Everyone born in Israel must follow these instructions when bringing Yahweh an offering through fire with a pleasing smell.
If a foreigner living with you, or anyone who lives among you in generations to come, wants to bring Yahweh such an offering, they’ll do it the same way you do.
In the assembly, the same rule applies to you and to the foreigner living with you, for every generation. Before Yahweh, the foreigner stands on the same terms as you.
The same law and instructions apply to you and the foreigner who lives among you.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you reach the land I’m bringing you to,
and start eating bread made from what the land grows, present a wave offering to Yahweh.
Make a cake from the first of your dough and present it as a wave offering. Lift it up the way you present the offering from the threshing floor.
Give Yahweh a wave offering from the first of your dough in every generation.
“‘Suppose you make a mistake and fail to follow any of these commands Yahweh spoke to Moses,
any of the commands Yahweh gave you through Moses, from the day he gave them onward through every generation.

If it happened by mistake without the community knowing, the whole community must give one young bull as a burnt offering with a smell pleasing to Yahweh, along with the required grain and drink offerings, and one male goat for a sin offering.

The priest will make atonement for the whole Israelite community, and they’ll be forgiven. It was a mistake, and they’ve brought Yahweh their offering through fire and their sin offering for that mistake.
The whole Israelite community will be forgiven, including the foreigners living among them, because the people as a whole did it without realizing it.
“‘If one person sins without realizing it, they’ll bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest will make atonement before Yahweh for the person who sinned by mistake. Once he’s made atonement for them, they’ll be forgiven.
Use the same law for anyone who does wrong by mistake, whether they were born in Israel or are a foreigner living among you.
“‘Anyone who does wrong in open defiance, whether born among you or a foreigner, insults Yahweh and will be cut off from their people.
They despised Yahweh’s word and broke his command, so they’ll be cut off completely. They’ll bear their own guilt.’”
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath.
The people who found him gathering sticks took him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
They held him in custody because nobody had been told what to do with him.
Yahweh told Moses, “The man must be put to death. The whole community will stone him outside the camp.”
The whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites to make tassels for the edges of their clothes in every generation. Put a blue cord on each tassel.
When you see the tassels, remember all Yahweh’s commands and do them. Don’t chase after what your heart and eyes want the way you used to, when you were unfaithful.
That way you’ll remember all my commands, put them into practice, and be holy to your God.
I’m Yahweh your God. I brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I’m Yahweh your God.”
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, joined up with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, from Reuben’s descendants. They gathered some men.
They rose up against Moses with 250 Israelites. These were well-known leaders of the community who were called to the assembly.

They came together against Moses and Aaron and said, “You’ve taken too much on yourselves. Everyone in this community is holy, and Yahweh is right here among them! Who put you above Yahweh’s assembly?”
When Moses heard that, he fell facedown.
He told Korah and his whole group, “In the morning, Yahweh will show who belongs to him and who is holy. He’ll let the person he chooses come near him.
Here’s what you’re going to do. Korah, you and your whole group, get your incense burners.
Tomorrow put fire and incense in them before Yahweh. The one Yahweh chooses is the one who’s holy. You Levites have gone too far!”
Moses told Korah, “Listen up, you descendants of Levi!
Does it mean so little to you that Israel’s God set you apart from the rest of Israel to bring you close to him, to work at Yahweh’s tabernacle, and to stand before the community and serve them?
He brought you close to him, along with all your fellow Levites. Now you want the priesthood too?
You and your whole group have gathered against Yahweh! Who is Aaron that you’re complaining about him?”
Moses sent for Eliab’s sons Dathan and Abiram. They said, “We’re not coming!
Wasn’t it enough that you took us out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in this wilderness? Now you have to make yourself our ruler too?
You haven’t brought us to any land flowing with milk and honey or given us fields and vineyards to inherit. Are you going to put these men’s eyes out? We’re not coming.”
Moses was furious. He told Yahweh, “Don’t accept their offering. I haven’t taken so much as one donkey from them, and I haven’t hurt any of them.”
Moses told Korah, “Tomorrow, come before Yahweh, you and your whole group, and Aaron too.
Each of your men must take his incense burner, put incense on it, and bring it before Yahweh. That’s 250 burners. You and Aaron each bring yours too.”
They each took their incense burner, put fire and incense in it, and stood at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting with Moses and Aaron.
Korah gathered the whole community against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh’s glory appeared to the entire assembly.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Get away from this assembly so I can consume them in an instant!”
They fell facedown and said, “God, God of the spirits of all living people, if one man sins, will you be angry with the whole assembly?”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the community, ‘Get away from the place where Korah, Dathan, and Abiram have their tents!’”
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram. Israel’s elders followed him.
He told the community, “Please step away from these wicked men’s tents. Don’t touch a thing that belongs to them, or their sins will get you swept away with them!”

So people backed away on every side from where Korah, Dathan, and Abiram lived. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
Moses said, “Here’s how you’ll know Yahweh sent me to do all this. These weren’t my own ideas.
If these men die like everyone else or go through what everyone else goes through, Yahweh didn’t send me.
But if Yahweh does something new and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them, so they go down alive into Sheol, you’ll know these men despised Yahweh.”
The moment Moses finished speaking, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, all of Korah’s men, and everything they owned.
They went down alive into Sheol with everything that belonged to them. The earth closed over them, and they were gone from the assembly.
The Israelites standing around them heard their screams and ran. “The earth might swallow us too!” they said.
Fire came out from Yahweh and consumed the 250 men who had offered incense.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to pick the incense burners out of the blaze and scatter the coals away from the camp. The burners are holy.

The men who used them sinned and paid with their lives. Hammer their burners into plates to cover the altar. They brought them before Yahweh, so the burners are holy. They’ll be a sign to the Israelites.”
Eleazar the priest took the bronze incense burners offered by the men who had burned. The burners were hammered flat to cover the altar.
It was a reminder to the Israelites: nobody outside Aaron’s family was to come near to burn incense before Yahweh and end up like Korah and his group. This was what Yahweh told Eleazar through Moses.
The next day the whole Israelite community complained against Moses and Aaron. “You killed Yahweh’s people!” they said.
When the community gathered against Moses and Aaron, they looked toward the Tent of Meeting. The cloud covered it, and Yahweh’s glory appeared.
Moses and Aaron came to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Get away from this assembly so I can consume them in an instant!” Moses and Aaron fell facedown.

Moses told Aaron, “Grab your incense burner. Put fire from the altar in it, add incense, and hurry to the assembly to make atonement for them. Yahweh’s anger has gone out. The plague has already started!”
Aaron did what Moses said and ran into the middle of the assembly. The plague was already spreading among the people. He put the incense on the fire and made atonement for them.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
The plague killed 14,700 people, apart from those who died in Korah’s rebellion.
Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. The plague had stopped.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites to give you twelve staffs, one from the leader of each ancestral family. Write each leader’s name on his own staff.
Write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff. There’s one staff for each head of an ancestral family.
Put them in the Tent of Meeting in front of the covenant, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout. That’s how I’ll put an end to the Israelites’ complaints against you that keep reaching me.”
Moses told the Israelites, and their leaders gave him one staff for each ancestral family, twelve staffs in all. Aaron’s staff was among them.
Moses placed the staffs before Yahweh in the Tent of the Testimony.
The next day Moses went into the Tent of the Testimony, and there it was: Aaron’s staff for Levi’s family had sprouted, formed buds, opened flowers, and grown ripe almonds.
Moses took all the staffs from before Yahweh and brought them out to the Israelites. They looked at them, and each man took his own staff.
Yahweh told Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back in front of the covenant. Keep it there as a warning to the rebels. Put an end to their complaints against me so they don’t die.”
Moses did exactly what Yahweh told him.
The Israelites told Moses, “Look at us! We’re dying! We’re ruined! Every one of us is ruined!
Anyone who gets close to Yahweh’s tabernacle dies! Are all of us going to die?”
Yahweh told Aaron, “You, your sons, and your ancestral family will bear the guilt for wrongs against the sanctuary. You and your sons will bear the guilt for wrongs in your priestly work.
Bring your fellow Levites, your father’s tribe, to join you and help you. You and your sons will serve in front of the Tent of the Testimony.
The Levites will follow your instructions and look after the whole tent. They must stay away from the sanctuary utensils and the altar, or both they and you will die.
They’ll work alongside you and take responsibility for everything that needs doing at the Tent of Meeting. No outsider may come near you.
“You’ll take care of the sanctuary and the altar so anger doesn’t fall on the Israelites again.
I myself took your fellow Levites from among the Israelites and gave them to you as a gift. They’re dedicated to Yahweh to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.

You and your sons will carry out your priestly duties in everything that concerns the altar and what’s behind the curtain. That’s your work. I’m giving you the priesthood as a gift. Any outsider who comes near must be put to death.”
Yahweh told Aaron, “I’ve put you in charge of my wave offerings, all the holy gifts the Israelites bring. Because you’ve been anointed, they’re your share and your sons’ share forever.

Here’s what’s yours from the most holy offerings kept back from the fire: every offering they bring me, including their grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings. Those are most holy for you and your sons.
Eat them as you would anything most holy. Every male in your family may eat them. Treat them as holy.

“The wave offerings from their gifts also belong to you. I’ve given all Israel’s wave offerings to you, your sons, and your daughters with you as your share forever. Anyone in your home who’s clean may eat them.
“I’ve given you the best of the oil, the wine, and the grain. Those are the first of the harvest they bring Yahweh.
The first ripe produce of everything that grows in their land, which they bring to Yahweh, belongs to you. Anyone in your home who’s clean may eat it.
“Everything permanently devoted in Israel belongs to you.
Every firstborn, human or animal, that they present to Yahweh belongs to you. But you must redeem every human firstborn and every firstborn of an unclean animal.
Redeem those that must be redeemed starting at one month old. Set the price at five silver shekels by the sanctuary standard, twenty gerahs to a shekel.
“Don’t redeem the firstborn of a cow, sheep, or goat. They’re holy. Splash their blood on the altar and burn their fat as an offering given through fire, with a smell pleasing to Yahweh.
Their meat belongs to you, just like the breast that’s waved and the right thigh.

I’ve given you and your sons and daughters all the holy gifts the Israelites present to Yahweh as wave offerings. That’s your share forever, a lasting covenant of salt before Yahweh for you and your descendants.”
Yahweh told Aaron, “You’ll get no inheritance in their land and no share among them. I’m your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
“I’ve given Levi’s descendants all the tithes in Israel as their inheritance for the work they do at the Tent of Meeting.
From now on the other Israelites must stay away from the Tent of Meeting, or they’ll become guilty and die.
The Levites will do the work at the Tent of Meeting, and they’ll bear the guilt for wrongs in that work. This rule stands for every generation. They’ll have no inheritance among the Israelites.
I’ve given the Levites the tithe the Israelites present to Yahweh as a wave offering. That’s their inheritance. That’s why I told them, ‘They’ll have no inheritance among the Israelites.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Levites, ‘When you receive the tithe I’ve given you from the Israelites as your inheritance, present Yahweh a wave offering from it: a tenth of the tenth.
Your wave offering will count as though you brought grain from your own threshing floor or wine from a full winepress.
That’s how you’ll present Yahweh a wave offering from every tithe you receive from the Israelites. Give Yahweh’s portion to Aaron the priest.
From everything you receive, set aside the best of it as the holy portion, and present it as Yahweh’s wave offering.’
“Tell them, ‘Once you’ve lifted up the best part, what’s left will count for you Levites as what comes from your own threshing floor and winepress.
You and your households can eat it anywhere. It’s your pay for working at the Tent of Meeting.
Once you’ve lifted up the best part, eating what’s left won’t make you guilty. Don’t treat the Israelites’ holy gifts with disrespect, or you’ll die.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Here’s the rule Yahweh has given. Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer with no spot or defect, one that’s never worn a yoke.
Give her to Eleazar the priest. He’ll take her outside the camp and have someone slaughter her right in front of him.
Eleazar the priest will take some of her blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Have someone burn the heifer where he can see it. Burn her hide, meat, blood, and dung.
The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet yarn and throw them into the middle of the fire where the heifer is burning.
Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He can come into camp after that, but he’ll be unclean until evening.
The person who burns the heifer must wash their clothes and bathe in water too. They’ll be unclean until evening.

“Someone who’s clean will collect the heifer’s ashes and store them in a clean place outside the camp. The Israelite community will keep them to use in water for cleansing impurity. It’s a sin offering.
The person who collects the ashes must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening. This rule lasts forever for the Israelites and the foreigners living among them.
“Anyone who touches a dead human body will be unclean for seven days.
They must cleanse themselves with the water on day three, and they’ll be clean on day seven. If they skip cleansing on day three, they’ll still be unclean on day seven.

Anyone who touches a dead person’s body and fails to cleanse themselves defiles Yahweh’s tabernacle. Cut that person off from Israel. The cleansing water wasn’t sprinkled on them, so their uncleanness remains.
“Here’s the rule when someone dies in a tent. Anyone who goes into the tent and anyone already inside will be unclean for seven days.
Any open container with no cover tied over it is unclean.
“Out in the open, anyone who touches someone killed by a sword, a dead body, a human bone, or a grave will be unclean for seven days.
“For the person who’s unclean, take some ashes from the burned sin offering, put them in a container, and pour running water over them.

Someone who’s clean will dip hyssop in the water and sprinkle it on the tent, the containers, the people who were there, and whoever touched the bone, the person who was killed, the dead body, or the grave.
The clean person will sprinkle the unclean person on day three and day seven. On day seven they’ll cleanse that person, who must wash their clothes and bathe in water. That evening they’ll be clean.
Anyone who’s unclean and refuses to cleanse themselves will be cut off from the assembly for defiling Yahweh’s sanctuary. They haven’t been sprinkled with the cleansing water, so they’re unclean.
This rule lasts forever. Anyone who sprinkles the cleansing water must wash their clothes, and anyone who touches the water will be unclean until evening.
“Anything an unclean person touches becomes unclean. Anyone who touches that thing will be unclean until evening.”
In the first month the whole Israelite community came into the wilderness of Zin and stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there, and that’s where she was buried.
There was no water for the community, so the people gathered against Moses and Aaron.
They argued with Moses. “If only we’d died when our brothers died before Yahweh!
Why bring Yahweh’s people into this wilderness just to have us and our animals die here?
Why drag us out of Egypt and bring us to this awful place? There’s nowhere to plant anything. There are no figs, grapevines, or pomegranates. There isn’t even water to drink!”
Moses and Aaron left the assembly, went to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and fell facedown. Yahweh’s glory appeared to them.
Yahweh told Moses:

“Take the staff. You and your brother Aaron, gather the community and speak to the rock while they watch. It’ll pour out its water. Bring water out of the rock for them so the people and their animals can drink.”
Moses took the staff from before Yahweh, just as he’d been told.
Moses and Aaron gathered the people in front of the rock. Moses told them, “Listen up, you rebels! Do we have to get water out of this rock for you?”
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out, and the people and their animals drank.
Yahweh told Moses and Aaron, “You didn’t trust me enough to show the Israelites that I’m holy. So you won’t lead this community into the land I’ve given them.”
Those were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with Yahweh and he showed himself holy among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom. “Here’s what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship we’ve been through.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived there for a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors.
When we cried out to Yahweh, he heard us, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Now we’re at Kadesh, a town right on the edge of your territory.

“Please let us cross your land. We won’t go through your fields or vineyards or drink from your wells. We’ll stick to the King’s Highway and won’t turn off to the right or left until we’ve crossed your border.”
Edom replied, “Don’t cross my land, or I’ll come out against you with the sword.”
The Israelites answered, “We’ll take the highway. If we or our livestock drink your water, we’ll pay for it. All we’re asking is to walk through.”
Edom’s king said, “You’re not crossing.” Edom came out against Israel with a large force and a show of strength.
Edom refused to let Israel cross its territory, so Israel turned away.
The whole Israelite community left Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, right by the border of Edom, Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Aaron will be gathered to his people. He won’t enter the land I’ve given the Israelites, because you rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.
Take off Aaron’s priestly clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people. He’ll die there.”
Moses did what Yahweh commanded. They climbed Mount Hor while the whole community watched.
Moses took off Aaron’s priestly clothes and put them on Eleazar. Aaron died there at the top of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came back down.
When the whole community saw that Aaron had died, all Israel mourned him for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the South. When he heard Israel was coming by the Atharim road, he fought them and took some of them prisoner.
Israel made a vow to Yahweh: “If you hand these people over to us, we’ll destroy their cities completely.”
Yahweh listened to Israel and handed over the Canaanites. Israel destroyed them and their cities completely. They called that place Hormah.
They left Mount Hor by the road to the Red Sea, going around Edom. The journey wore the people down.
They spoke against God and Moses. “Why bring us out of Egypt just to die in the wilderness? We have no bread and no water. We can’t stand this disgusting food!”
Yahweh sent venomous snakes among the people. The snakes bit them, and many Israelites died.
The people went to Moses and said, “We sinned when we spoke against Yahweh and against you. Pray to Yahweh to take these snakes away from us.” So Moses prayed for them.
Yahweh told Moses, “Make a venomous snake and put it on a pole. Anyone who’s bitten and looks at it will live.”
Moses made a bronze snake and put it on the pole. Whenever someone was bitten, they looked at the bronze snake and lived.
The Israelites traveled on and camped at Oboth.
They left Oboth and camped at Iyeabarim, in the wilderness east of Moab, toward the sunrise.
From there they went on and camped in the Zered Valley.
Then they camped on the far side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that stretches out from Amorite territory. The Arnon marks the border between Moab and the Amorites.
That’s why the Book of the Wars of Yahweh says, “Vaheb in Suphah, the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slope of the valleys that runs toward Ar and lies against the border of Moab.”
From there they went to Beer, the well where Yahweh told Moses, “Gather the people together, and I’ll give them water.”
