Then Israel sang this song: “Well, spring up! Sing to it,
the well the leaders dug, the one the people’s nobles dug with their scepter and their staffs.” From the wilderness they traveled to Mattanah.
From Mattanah they went to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
From Bamoth they went to the valley in Moab’s countryside, to the top of Pisgah overlooking the desert.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon, the Amorite king:
“Let us cross your land. We won’t turn into anyone’s fields or vineyards or drink from the wells. We’ll stay on the King’s Highway till we’ve crossed your border.”
Sihon refused to let Israel cross his territory. He called all his people together, marched out into the wilderness against Israel, and fought them at Jahaz.
Israel defeated him by the sword and took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, whose border was fortified.
Israel took all those towns and settled in the Amorite towns, including Heshbon and all its surrounding villages.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites. He’d fought the previous king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.
That’s why the people who speak in proverbs say, “Come to Heshbon. Build up Sihon’s city and make it stand strong.
Fire went out from Heshbon, flames from Sihon’s city. It consumed Ar in Moab and the rulers of the heights along the Arnon.
You’re in trouble, Moab! You’re done for, people of Chemosh! He’s let his sons become fugitives and handed his daughters over as captives to Sihon, king of the Amorites.
We shot at them. Heshbon is gone all the way to Dibon. We laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”
That’s how Israel came to live in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to scout Jazer. They captured its villages and drove out the Amorites living there.
They turned and went up the road to Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with all his people to fight them at Edrei.
Yahweh told Moses, “Don’t be afraid of him. I’ve handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
So they struck down Og, his sons, and all his people. Nobody survived, and Israel took possession of his land.
The Israelites traveled on and set up camp on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified because there were so many Israelites. The whole country was shaken.
The Moabites told Midian’s elders, “This crowd will lick up everything around us like an ox licking up the grass in a field.” Balak son of Zippor was Moab’s king at the time.
He sent messengers to call Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, by the River, in his home country. “Look, a whole people has come out of Egypt. They cover the land and have settled right across from me.
Please come and curse them for me. They’re too strong for me. Maybe then I can beat them and drive them out of the land. I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and Midian left with payment for the divination and went to Balaam. They gave him Balak’s message.
Balaam told them, “Stay here tonight. I’ll tell you what Yahweh says to me.” So Moab’s leaders stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men staying with you?”
Balaam told God, “Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, sent me this message:
‘Look, these people came out of Egypt and cover the land. Come curse them for me. Maybe then I’ll be able to fight them and drive them out.’”
God told Balaam, “Don’t go with them. Don’t curse those people. They’re blessed.”
In the morning Balaam got up and told Balak’s leaders, “Go home. Yahweh won’t let me go with you.”
Moab’s leaders got up, went back to Balak, and said, “Balaam won’t come with us.”
Balak sent another group of leaders, more than before and with higher standing.
They went to Balaam and said, “Here’s what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please don’t let anything stop you from coming to me.
I’ll honor you greatly and do whatever you tell me. Please come and curse these people for me.’”
Balaam answered Balak’s servants, “Balak could give me his house packed with silver and gold, and I still couldn’t go beyond the word of Yahweh my God in anything, big or small.
But please stay here tonight too, so I can find out what else Yahweh has to say to me.”
God came to Balaam in the night and said, “If these men have come to call you, get up and go with them. Do only what I tell you.”
In the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with Moab’s leaders.
God was furious that Balaam went, and Yahweh’s angel stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants along.
The donkey saw Yahweh’s angel standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. She turned off the road and went into a field. Balaam hit her to get her back on the road.
Then Yahweh’s angel stood in a narrow path between vineyards, with a wall on each side.
When the donkey saw Yahweh’s angel, she pressed herself against the wall and crushed Balaam’s foot against it. He hit her again.
Yahweh’s angel went farther ahead and stood in a tight spot where there was nowhere to turn, right or left.
The donkey saw Yahweh’s angel and lay down with Balaam still on her back. Balaam lost his temper and hit her with his staff.
Yahweh opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What did I do to you that made you hit me three times?”
Balaam told the donkey, “You made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I’d kill you right now.”
The donkey said, “Haven’t I been your donkey all your life, the one you’ve ridden up to this very day? Have I ever acted like this with you before?” He said, “No.”
Then Yahweh opened Balaam’s eyes. He saw Yahweh’s angel standing in the road, holding a drawn sword. Balaam bowed his head and fell facedown.
Yahweh’s angel said, “Why did you hit your donkey those three times? I came out to oppose you because the road you’re taking is wrong in my eyes.
The donkey saw me and turned away from me those three times. If she hadn’t turned away, I’d have killed you by now and let her live.”
Balaam told Yahweh’s angel, “I’ve sinned. I didn’t know you were standing in the road to stop me. If you don’t want me to go, I’ll turn back.”
Yahweh’s angel told Balaam, “Go with the men, but say only what I tell you to say.” So Balaam went on with Balak’s leaders.
When Balak heard Balaam had arrived, he went out to meet him at the City of Moab, on the Arnon, at the far edge of his territory.
Balak asked Balaam, “Didn’t I send you an urgent invitation? Why didn’t you come? Don’t you think I can give you a place of honor?”
Balaam answered, “Look, I’m here now. But do I have any power to say whatever I want? I’ll say whatever God puts in my mouth.”
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath Huzoth.
Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and sent portions to Balaam and the leaders with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam up to the high places of Baal. From there Balaam could see part of the people.
Balaam told Balak, “Build me seven altars here and get seven bulls and seven rams ready.”
Balak did what Balaam asked. Together they offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said, “Stay here by your burnt offering while I go. Maybe Yahweh will come and meet me. Whatever he shows me, I’ll tell you.” Then he went to a bare hilltop.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said, “I’ve set up seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each one.”
Yahweh put a message in Balaam’s mouth and told him, “Go back to Balak and give him this message.”
When Balaam got back, Balak was standing by his burnt offering with all the leaders of Moab.
Balaam began his oracle: “Balak brought me from Aram, Moab’s king called me from the eastern mountains. ‘Come curse Jacob for me. Come denounce Israel.’
How can I curse people God hasn’t cursed? How can I denounce people Yahweh hasn’t denounced?
I see them from the rocky heights. I look down on them from the hills. There’s a people who live apart and aren’t counted among the nations.
Who could count Jacob’s people, as numerous as dust, or count even a quarter of Israel? Let me die like the righteous, and let my end be like theirs!”
Balak told Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and you’ve gone and blessed them!”
Balaam answered, “Don’t I have to be careful to say what Yahweh puts in my mouth?”
Balak said, “Come with me to another spot where you can see them. You’ll see just part of them from there. Curse them for me from that spot.”
He took Balaam to the field of Zophim at the top of Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each one.
Balaam told Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offering while I go over there to meet God.”
Yahweh met Balaam, put a message in his mouth, and said, “Go back to Balak and say this.”
Balaam went back. Balak was standing by his burnt offering with the leaders of Moab. Balak asked, “What did Yahweh say?”
Balaam began his oracle: “Get up, Balak, and listen! Hear me, son of Zippor.
God isn’t human, so he doesn’t lie. He isn’t a human being who changes his mind. Would he say something and fail to do it? Would he speak and fail to carry it out?
Look, I’ve been told to bless. God has blessed them, and there’s no undoing it.
He hasn’t seen wrongdoing in Jacob or found anything crooked in Israel. Yahweh their God is with them, and the shout of a king rings out among them.
God brings them out of Egypt. He has strength like a wild ox.
There’s no enchantment with Jacob and no divination with Israel. Now people will say about Jacob and Israel, ‘Look what God has done!’
Look at this people rise like a lioness, stand up like a lion! They won’t lie down until they’ve eaten their prey and drunk the blood of those they killed.”
Balak told Balaam, “If you won’t curse them, don’t bless them either.”
Balaam answered, “Didn’t I tell you I have to do everything Yahweh says?”
Balak said, “Come on, I’ll take you somewhere else. Maybe God will let you curse them for me from there.”
Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, overlooking the desert.
Balaam told Balak, “Build me seven altars here and get seven bulls and seven rams ready.”
Balak did what Balaam asked and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam saw that Yahweh was pleased to bless Israel. This time he skipped the divination he’d used before and turned toward the wilderness.
Balaam looked up and saw Israel camped by tribe, and God’s Spirit came on him.
He began his oracle: “These are the words of Balaam son of Beor, the man whose eyes are open.
These are the words of the man who hears God speak, who sees the Almighty’s vision and falls down with his eyes open:
How beautiful your tents are, Jacob! How beautiful your homes are, Israel!
They stretch out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloe trees Yahweh planted, like cedars beside the water.
Water will spill from his buckets, and his seed will have plenty of water. His king will rise higher than Agag, and his kingdom will be lifted high.
God brings him out of Egypt. He has strength like a wild ox. He’ll devour the nations that oppose him, shatter their bones, and pierce them with his arrows.
He crouches and lies down like a lion, like a lioness. Who’d dare wake him? Everyone who blesses you is blessed. Everyone who curses you is cursed.”
Balak was furious with Balaam and slammed his hands together. “I called you here to curse my enemies, and you’ve done nothing but bless them all three times!
Get out of here and go home! I was going to give you great honor, but look, Yahweh has kept it from you.”
Balaam told Balak, “Didn’t I tell the messengers you sent to me,
‘Even if Balak gave me his house packed with silver and gold, I couldn’t go beyond Yahweh’s word and do good or bad on my own. I’ll say what Yahweh says’?
I’m going back to my people now. Come here and I’ll tell you what these people will do to yours in days to come.”
He began his oracle: “These are the words of Balaam son of Beor, the man whose eyes are open.
These are the words of the man who hears God speak, who knows what the Most High makes known, who sees the Almighty’s vision and falls down with his eyes open:

I see him, but it isn’t now. I catch sight of him, but he isn’t near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise from Israel and smash through the corners of Moab and crush all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will be taken. So will Seir, his enemy, while Israel fights bravely.
Someone from Jacob will rule and destroy the survivors from the city.”
Balaam looked at Amalek and began his oracle: “Amalek was first among the nations, but in the end he’ll be destroyed.”
He looked at the Kenites and began his oracle: “You live in a strong place. Your nest is set in the rock.
Even so, Kain will be laid waste, until Asshur takes you away captive.”
He began another oracle: “Oh, who will survive when God does this?
Ships will come from the coast of Kittim. They’ll oppress Asshur and Eber, and he too will come to ruin.”
Then Balaam got up and went back home, and Balak went his own way.
Israel stayed at Shittim. The people started sleeping with Moabite women and being unfaithful.
The women invited them to sacrifices for their gods. The Israelites ate the food and bowed down to those gods.
Israel attached itself to Baal of Peor, and Yahweh’s anger flared against Israel.
Yahweh told Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and hang them up before Yahweh in broad daylight so Yahweh’s fierce anger will turn away from Israel.”
Moses told Israel’s judges, “Each of you must put to death the men under you who joined themselves to Baal of Peor.”
Then an Israelite brought a Midianite woman to his people in full view of Moses and the whole Israelite community. They were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron the priest, saw it, he got up from among the people and took a spear.
He followed the Israelite man into the tent and drove the spear through both the man and the woman’s body. Then the plague among the Israelites stopped.
The plague killed 24,000 people.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Phinehas son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron the priest, turned my anger away from the Israelites. He shared my zeal among them, so in my zeal I didn’t wipe them out.
So tell him, ‘I’m giving him my covenant of peace.
It’ll be a covenant of lasting priesthood for him and his descendants, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.’”
The Israelite killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the head of an ancestral family in Simeon.
The Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur. He led an ancestral family in Midian.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Treat the Midianites as enemies and strike them.

They treated you as enemies with their tricks. They fooled you in what happened at Peor and in what happened with their own Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader. She was killed on the day of the plague at Peor.”
After the plague, Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest:
“Take a census of the whole Israelite community by ancestral family. Count everyone in Israel who’s twenty or older and able to go to war.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke to them on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
“Count everyone twenty or older, just as Yahweh told Moses and the Israelites.” These are the people who came out of Egypt.
Reuben was Israel’s firstborn. From his sons came the Hanochite clan through Hanoch and the Palluite clan through Pallu.
Hezron gave rise to the Hezronite clan, and Carmi to the Carmite clan.
Those were Reuben’s clans. The count came to 43,730.
Pallu’s son was Eliab.
Eliab’s sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were the same Dathan and Abiram called to the assembly who joined Korah’s group in rebelling against Moses and Aaron. They rebelled against Yahweh.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up with Korah when his group died. Fire consumed 250 men, and what happened to them became a warning.
Korah’s sons, though, didn’t die.
Simeon’s sons by clan: Nemuel gave rise to the Nemuelites, Jamin to the Jaminites, and Jachin to the Jachinites.
Zerah gave rise to the Zerahites, and Shaul to the Shaulites.
Those were Simeon’s clans, with a total of 22,200.
Gad’s sons by clan: Zephon gave rise to the Zephonites, Haggi to the Haggites, and Shuni to the Shunites.
Ozni gave rise to the Oznites, and Eri to the Erites.
Arod gave rise to the Arodites, and Areli to the Arelites.
Those were the clans of Gad’s descendants. The count came to 40,500.
Judah’s sons included Er and Onan. Both died in Canaan.
Judah’s sons by clan: Shelah gave rise to the Shelanites, Perez to the Perezites, and Zerah to the Zerahites.
From Perez’s sons came the Hezronite clan through Hezron and the Hamulite clan through Hamul.
Those were Judah’s clans. The count came to 76,500.
Issachar’s sons by clan: Tola gave rise to the Tolaites and Puvah to the Punites.
Jashub gave rise to the Jashubites, and Shimron to the Shimronites.
Those were Issachar’s clans. The count came to 64,300.
Zebulun’s sons by clan: Sered gave rise to the Seredites, Elon to the Elonites, and Jahleel to the Jahleelites.
Those were Zebulun’s clans. The count came to 60,500.
Joseph’s sons by clan were Manasseh and Ephraim.
From Manasseh’s line came the Machirite clan through Machir. Machir was Gilead’s father, and Gilead gave rise to the Gileadites.
Gilead’s sons included Iezer, whose clan was the Iezerites, and Helek, whose clan was the Helekites.
Asriel gave rise to the Asrielites, and Shechem to the Shechemites.
Shemida gave rise to the Shemidaites, and Hepher to the Hepherites.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had daughters and no sons. His daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Those were Manasseh’s clans. The count came to 52,700.
Ephraim’s sons by clan: Shuthelah gave rise to the Shuthelahites, Becher to the Becherites, and Tahan to the Tahanites.
From Shuthelah’s sons came the Eranite clan through Eran.
Those were the clans of Ephraim’s descendants. The count came to 32,500. That’s Joseph’s line by clan.
Benjamin’s sons by clan: Bela gave rise to the Belaites, Ashbel to the Ashbelites, and Ahiram to the Ahiramites.
Shephupham gave rise to the Shuphamites, and Hupham to the Huphamites.
Bela’s sons were Ard and Naaman, whose clans were the Ardites and the Naamites.
Those were Benjamin’s descendants by clan. The count came to 45,600.
Dan’s descendants by clan came through Shuham, whose clan was the Shuhamites. Those were Dan’s clans.
The count of all the Shuhamite clans came to 64,400.
Asher’s sons by clan: Imnah gave rise to the Imnites, Ishvi to the Ishvites, and Beriah to the Berites.
From Beriah’s sons came the Heberites through Heber and the Malchielites through Malchiel.
Asher’s daughter was named Serah.
Those were the clans of Asher’s descendants. The count came to 53,400.
Naphtali’s sons by clan: Jahzeel gave rise to the Jahzeelites, and Guni to the Gunites.
Jezer gave rise to the Jezerites, and Shillem to the Shillemites.
Those were Naphtali’s clans. The count came to 45,400.
The total counted in Israel was 601,730.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Divide the land among these people as their inheritance, using the number of names on the list.
Give larger groups a bigger share and smaller groups a smaller share. Each group will get its inheritance according to the number counted in it.
The land itself must be divided by drawing lots. They’ll inherit it under the names of their ancestral tribes.
The lot will decide where their inheritance falls, whether the group is large or small.”
These were the Levites counted by clan: the Gershonites through Gershon, the Kohathites through Kohath, and the Merarites through Merari.
Levi’s clans included the Libnites, Hebronites, Mahlites, Mushites, and Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram.
Amram’s wife was Jochebed, Levi’s daughter, born to him in Egypt. She had Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam with Amram.
Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they brought unauthorized fire before Yahweh.
The Levite count came to 23,000, every male a month old or older. They were counted apart from the other Israelites because they weren’t given a land inheritance among them.
That’s who Moses and Eleazar the priest counted when they took Israel’s census on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
No man in that count had been counted by Moses and Aaron the priest in the earlier Israelite census in the Sinai wilderness.
Yahweh had said of those men, “They’ll die in the wilderness.” None of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Zelophehad’s daughters stepped forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of Joseph’s son Manasseh. His daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole community. They said,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He wasn’t part of Korah’s group that gathered against Yahweh. He died for his own sin, and he left no sons.
Why should our father’s name disappear from his family just because he had no son? Give us land of our own among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before Yahweh.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Zelophehad’s daughters are right. Give them a share of the land among their father’s brothers. Pass their father’s inheritance on to them.
Tell the Israelites, ‘If a man dies without a son, pass his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, give it to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give it to his father’s brothers.
If his father has no brothers, give it to his closest relative in the clan. That relative will take possession of it. This is a binding rule for the Israelites, as Yahweh commanded Moses.’”
Yahweh told Moses, “Go up this mountain in Abarim and look at the land I’ve given the Israelites.
After you see it, you’ll be gathered to your people, just like your brother Aaron.

You rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Zin when the community quarreled. You failed to show them that I’m holy there at the waters, right in front of them.” Those were the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.
Moses spoke to Yahweh:
“May Yahweh, the God of the spirits of all living people, put a man in charge of the community.
Let him go out in front of them and come back in front of them. Let him lead them out and bring them back in, so Yahweh’s community won’t be like sheep without a shepherd.”
Yahweh told Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man who has the Spirit in him, and lay your hand on him.
Stand him before Eleazar the priest and the whole community, and commission him while they watch.
Give him authority so the whole Israelite community will obey him.

Joshua will stand before Eleazar the priest, who will ask Yahweh for a decision on his behalf using the Urim. At his word Joshua and all the Israelites with him will go out, and at his word the whole community will come in.”
Moses did exactly what Yahweh told him. He took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and the whole community.
He laid his hands on Joshua and commissioned him, just as Yahweh had said through Moses.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Make sure you bring my offerings at the right time. They’re my food, given through fire, with a smell that pleases me.’
Tell them, ‘Here’s what you’ll offer Yahweh through fire every day: two year-old male lambs with no defects for the regular burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other in the evening.
With it, bring a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from crushed olives.
This is the regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai, given to Yahweh through fire with a pleasing smell.
With each lamb, bring a quarter of a hin as a drink offering. Pour out strong drink for Yahweh in the holy place.
Offer the second lamb in the evening with the same grain and drink offerings as in the morning. It’s an offering given through fire, with a smell that pleases Yahweh.
“‘On the Sabbath, offer two year-old male lambs with no defects, a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and the drink offering that goes with it.
That’s the burnt offering for each Sabbath, on top of the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
“‘At the start of each month, bring Yahweh a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs with no defects.
For each bull, offer three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. For the ram, offer two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil.
For each lamb, give a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. This burnt offering is given to Yahweh through fire, with a pleasing smell.
For the drink offerings, bring half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. That’s the burnt offering for each month of the year.
Also bring Yahweh one male goat as a sin offering, on top of the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
“‘Yahweh’s Passover falls on day fourteen of month one.
Day fifteen of that same month starts the festival. Eat bread made without yeast for seven days.
On the first day, have a holy gathering and lay aside your regular work.
Bring Yahweh a burnt offering through fire: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs, all without defects.
Bring their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for each bull and two tenths for the ram.
Bring a tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs,
and one male goat for a sin offering to make atonement for you.
Bring these on top of the morning burnt offering, which is part of the regular burnt offering.
For seven days, bring this food as an offering to Yahweh through fire every day, with a smell that pleases him. It’s on top of the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
Hold a holy gathering on day seven and lay aside your regular work.
“‘On the day you bring the first of the harvest, when you present Yahweh the new grain offering at your Festival of Weeks, hold a holy gathering and lay aside your regular work.
Bring a burnt offering with a smell pleasing to Yahweh: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs.
Bring fine flour mixed with oil as their grain offering: three tenths of an ephah for each bull, two tenths for the ram,
and a tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Bring one male goat to make atonement for you.
Bring them and their drink offerings on top of the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. Make sure the animals have no defects.
“‘On day one of month seven, hold a holy gathering. Set aside your regular work. It’s a day to blow the trumpets. 🎺
Bring a burnt offering with a smell that pleases Yahweh: one young bull, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring fine flour mixed with oil as their grain offering: three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.

These come on top of the new moon burnt offering with its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering. Bring their drink offerings as prescribed. It’s an offering given to Yahweh through fire, with a pleasing smell.
“‘On day ten of this seventh month, hold a holy gathering. Deny yourselves and do no work at all.
Bring Yahweh a burnt offering with a pleasing smell: one young bull, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
Bring fine flour mixed with oil as their grain offering: three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, on top of the sin offering for atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
“‘On day fifteen of month seven, hold a holy gathering and set aside your regular work. Celebrate a festival for Yahweh for seven days.
Give a burnt offering through fire with a smell pleasing to Yahweh: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
Bring fine flour mixed with oil as their grain offering: three tenths for each of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each of the two rams,
and one tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day two, bring twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day three, bring eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day four, bring ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day five, bring nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day six, bring eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day seven, bring seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.
“‘On day eight, hold a solemn gathering. Set aside your regular work.
Give Yahweh a burnt offering through fire, with a smell that pleases him: one bull, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs with no defects.
Bring the grain and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, in the amounts required for each animal.
Bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.

“‘Bring these burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings to Yahweh at your appointed festivals, on top of the offerings you’ve vowed to give and the ones you give freely.’”
Moses told the Israelites everything Yahweh had commanded him.
Moses spoke to the heads of Israel’s tribes: “Here’s what Yahweh has commanded.
When a man makes a vow to Yahweh or takes an oath that binds him to a pledge, he must keep his word. He must do everything he said he’d do.
“Suppose a young woman still living in her father’s house makes a vow to Yahweh and binds herself with a pledge.
If her father hears what she vowed or pledged and says nothing to her, all her vows and every pledge she made still stand.
If her father forbids her on the day he hears about it, none of her vows or binding pledges stand. Yahweh will forgive her because her father forbade her.
“Suppose she gets married while still bound by a vow or a promise she blurted out without thinking.
If her husband hears about it and says nothing to her that day, her vows and all her binding pledges still stand.
But if he forbids her the day he hears about it, he cancels the vow or the hurried promise that bound her. Yahweh will forgive her.
“A widow or a divorced woman must keep every vow she’s bound herself to.
“Suppose a woman makes a vow in her husband’s house or takes an oath that binds her to a pledge.
If her husband hears about it and keeps quiet instead of forbidding her, every vow and binding pledge she made still stands.
But if he cancels them on the day he hears about them, none of the vows or pledges she spoke will stand. Her husband canceled them, and Yahweh will forgive her.
Her husband can confirm or cancel any vow or binding oath she makes to deny herself.
If her husband keeps saying nothing day after day, all the vows and pledges binding her still stand. His silence on the day he heard about them confirmed them.
If he cancels them later, after he’s heard about them, he’ll bear her guilt.”
Those are the rules Yahweh gave Moses for a man and his wife, and for a father and his young daughter while she’s living in his house.
Yahweh told Moses:
“Take vengeance on the Midianites for what they did to the Israelites. After that, you’ll be gathered to your people.”
Moses told the people, “Get some of your men armed for battle. They’ll go against Midian to carry out Yahweh’s vengeance.
Send a thousand men to the war from each tribe of Israel.”
So from Israel’s thousands they supplied a thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand men armed for war.
Moses sent a thousand men from each tribe into battle with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas carried the holy utensils and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought Midian as Yahweh had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
Among those they killed were Midian’s five kings: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took the Midianite women and their children captive. They took all their livestock, flocks, and possessions as plunder.
They burned every town where the Midianites lived and all their camps.
They took all the captives and all the spoils, people and animals alike.
They brought the captives and everything they’d taken to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the Israelite community. The camp was on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the community’s leaders went outside the camp to meet them.
Moses was angry with the army officers who came back from battle, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.
He asked them, “You kept all the women alive?
These are the women who acted on Balaam’s advice and led the Israelites to betray Yahweh at Peor. That’s why the plague struck Yahweh’s community.
So now kill every boy and every woman who has slept with a man.
Keep alive for yourselves the girls who have never slept with a man.
“Stay outside the camp for seven days. Anyone who killed someone or touched a dead body must cleanse themselves on day three and day seven. That goes for you and your captives.
Cleanse all the clothes, everything made of leather or goat hair, and everything made of wood.”
Eleazar the priest told the men who’d gone into battle, “Here’s the rule Yahweh gave Moses.
Take all the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead,
and pass through fire whatever can stand the heat. It’ll be clean, but it must also be cleansed with the water for impurity. Whatever can’t stand the fire must go through the water.
Wash your clothes on day seven, and you’ll be clean. Then you can come into camp.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“You, Eleazar the priest, and the community’s ancestral family heads must count the plunder, both the people and the animals.
Split it in half between the men who went out to fight and the whole community.
Collect a tribute for Yahweh from the men who fought. Take one out of every five hundred from the people, cattle, donkeys, and flocks.
Take it out of the fighters’ half and give it to Eleazar the priest as Yahweh’s wave offering.
From the Israelites’ half, take one out of every fifty, whether people, cattle, donkeys, sheep, goats, or any other livestock. Give them to the Levites who take care of Yahweh’s tabernacle.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest did what Yahweh had commanded Moses.
Apart from what the fighters took for themselves, the plunder came to 675,000 sheep,
72,000 head of cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 women in all who had never slept with a man.
The half for those who’d gone to war came to 337,500 sheep.
Yahweh’s tribute from the sheep was 675.
There were 36,000 head of cattle. Yahweh’s tribute was 72.
There were 30,500 donkeys. Yahweh’s tribute was 61.
There were 16,000 people. Yahweh’s tribute was 32 people.
Moses gave the tribute to Eleazar the priest as Yahweh’s wave offering, just as Yahweh had commanded him.
Moses set the Israelites’ half apart from the share of the men who fought.
The community’s half came to 337,500 sheep,
36,000 head of cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.
From that half Moses took one out of every fifty, people and animals alike, and gave them to the Levites who took care of Yahweh’s tabernacle. He did what Yahweh had commanded him.
The army officers who led the thousands and the hundreds came to Moses.
They said, “Your servants have counted the fighting men under our command. We aren’t missing a single man.
We’ve brought Yahweh an offering from what each man found: gold ornaments, armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for our lives before Yahweh.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted their gold, all of it worked jewelry.
All the gold the commanders of thousands and hundreds lifted up as an offering to Yahweh weighed 16,750 shekels.
The fighting men had each taken plunder for themselves.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and hundreds into the Tent of Meeting as a reminder of the Israelites before Yahweh.
Reuben’s and Gad’s descendants had huge herds. When they saw Jazer and Gilead, they could tell the land was good for livestock.
So the people of Gad and Reuben came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community. They said,
“Look at Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon.
This land Yahweh struck down before Israel’s community is good for livestock, and your servants have plenty of livestock.”
They went on, “If we’ve found favor with you, give us this land to own. Please don’t make us cross the Jordan.”
Moses told Gad and Reuben, “Are your brothers supposed to go to war while you sit here?
Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land Yahweh gave them?
That’s what your ancestors did when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to look at the land.
They went up to the valley of Eshcol and saw the land. Then they talked Israel out of going into the land Yahweh had given them.
Yahweh’s anger flared that day, and he swore:
‘None of the men who came out of Egypt at twenty or older will see the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. They didn’t follow me wholeheartedly.
The exceptions are Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun. They followed Yahweh wholeheartedly.’
Yahweh was angry with Israel and made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until that whole generation that did evil in his sight was gone.
“Now look at you, a new crop of sinners stepping into your ancestors’ place and making Yahweh even angrier with Israel.
If you turn away from him, he’ll leave Israel in the wilderness again, and you’ll bring ruin on all these people.”
They came closer and said, “We’ll build sheep pens here for our livestock and towns for our children.
Then we’ll arm ourselves and go at the front of the Israelites until we’ve brought them to their own land. Our children will stay in fortified towns for protection from the people living here.
We won’t go home until all the Israelites have received their inheritance.
We won’t ask for land with them past the other side of the Jordan. Our inheritance is here on the east side.”
Moses told them, “Here’s the deal. If you arm yourselves for battle before Yahweh,
and all your armed men cross the Jordan before him and stay until he’s driven out his enemies,
and the land has been brought under control before Yahweh, then you can come back. You’ll have done your duty to Yahweh and Israel, and this land will be yours before Yahweh.
“But if you don’t follow through, you’ll have sinned against Yahweh. You can be sure your sin will catch up with you.
Build towns for your children and pens for your sheep. Then do what you said you’d do.”
The people of Gad and Reuben told Moses, “Your servants will do what you command, my lord.
Our children, wives, flocks, and all our other livestock will stay in the towns of Gilead.
But every one of your servants armed for war will cross over to fight before Yahweh, just as you say, my lord.”
Moses passed those instructions on to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the ancestral family heads of Israel’s tribes.
He told them, “If all the armed men of Gad and Reuben cross the Jordan with you to fight before Yahweh, and the land is brought under control before you, give them Gilead to own.
If they won’t cross armed with you, they’ll receive land among you in Canaan.”
The people of Gad and Reuben answered, “We’ll do just what Yahweh told your servants.
We’ll cross armed before Yahweh into Canaan. The land we inherit across the Jordan will stay ours.”

Moses gave the people of Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdoms of Sihon, the Amorite king, and Og, the king of Bashan. He gave them the land, its towns within their borders, and the towns around them.
Gad’s descendants built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran. They built fortified towns and sheep pens.
Reuben’s descendants built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo and Baal Meon, whose names were changed, and Sibmah. They gave new names to the towns they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, took it, and drove out the Amorites living there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and took its villages and called them Havvoth Jair.
Nobah went and took Kenath and its villages. He named it Nobah after himself.
Here’s the route the Israelites took when they marched out of Egypt by divisions under Moses and Aaron.
At Yahweh’s command Moses wrote down where they started each leg of the journey. These are the stages, listed by where each one began.
They left Rameses on day fifteen of the first month. It was the day after Passover, and the Israelites marched out boldly where all the Egyptians could see them.
The Egyptians were burying the firstborn Yahweh had struck down among them. Yahweh had also judged their gods.
The Israelites left Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They left Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.
They left Etham and turned back toward Pihahiroth, across from Baal Zephon. They camped in front of Migdol.
They left the area in front of Hahiroth and went right through the sea into the wilderness. After three days in the wilderness of Etham, they camped at Marah.
They left Marah and came to Elim. There were twelve springs and seventy palm trees at Elim, so they camped there.
They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They left the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They left the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They left Alush and camped at Rephidim. There was no drinking water for the people there.
They left Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They left the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
They left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez.
They left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.
They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
They left Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.
They left Bene Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.
They left Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.
They left Ezion Geber and camped at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor on the edge of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at Yahweh’s command and died there. It was day one of month five, forty years after the Israelites came out of Egypt.
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the South of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
They left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim on Moab’s border.
They left Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad.
They left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim.
They left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim in front of Nebo.
They left the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Their camp along the Jordan stretched from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim on the plains of Moab.
Yahweh spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
drive out everyone who lives in the land ahead of you. Smash all their stone idols and their metal images, and tear down every one of their worship sites on the heights.
Take possession of the land and live there. I’ve given it to you to own.

Draw lots to divide the land among your clans. Give larger groups a bigger share and smaller groups a smaller share. Wherever a person’s lot falls, that’s their land. Inherit it according to your ancestral tribes.
“‘But if you leave any of the people living there, they’ll be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They’ll give you trouble in the land where you live.
Then what I planned to do to them, I’ll do to you.’”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Give the Israelites these instructions: ‘When you enter Canaan, here are the borders of the land you’ll receive as your inheritance.
Your southern territory will stretch from the wilderness of Zin along Edom. On its eastern end, the southern border will start at the end of the Salt Sea.
The border will curve south of the ascent of Akrabbim and pass through Zin. It’ll go south of Kadesh Barnea, then run to Hazar Addar and on to Azmon.
From Azmon it’ll turn toward the brook of Egypt and end at the sea.
“‘On the west, the Great Sea and its coastline will be your border.
“‘Here’s your northern border. Mark it out from the Great Sea to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor, mark it out to the entrance of Hamath. The border will pass by Zedad.
Then it’ll go to Ziphron and end at Hazar Enan. That’s your northern border.
“‘Mark out your eastern border from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
From Shepham the border will go down to Riblah, east of Ain. Then it’ll go down to the eastern shore of the Sea of Chinnereth.
The border will follow the Jordan down to the Salt Sea, where it ends. Those are the borders all the way around your land.’”
Moses told the Israelites, “This is the land you’ll inherit by drawing lots. Yahweh has commanded that it go to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad have already received their inheritance by ancestral family, and so has the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Those two tribes and the half-tribe received their land across the Jordan from Jericho, on the east side toward the sunrise.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Here are the men who’ll divide the land among you for your inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Choose one leader from each tribe to help divide the land.
Here are their names. From Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From Simeon: Shemuel son of Ammihud.
From Benjamin: Elidad son of Chislon.
From Dan: Bukki son of Jogli, their leader.
From Joseph’s descendants, for Manasseh: Hanniel son of Ephod, their leader.
From Ephraim: Kemuel son of Shiphtan, their leader.
From Zebulun: Elizaphan son of Parnach, their leader.
From Issachar: Paltiel son of Azzan, their leader.
From Asher: Ahihud son of Shelomi, their leader.
From Naphtali: Pedahel son of Ammihud, their leader.”
These were the men Yahweh told to divide the land of Canaan among the Israelites for their inheritance.
Yahweh spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
“Tell the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in out of the land they inherit. Give them the pastureland around those towns too.
The towns will be their homes, and the pastureland will be for their livestock, their possessions, and all their other animals.
“The pastureland you give the Levites will stretch a thousand cubits out from the town wall all the way around.

Measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the town in the middle. That will be the pastureland for their towns.
“Give the Levites six towns of refuge where someone who kills a person can run for safety. Give them forty-two other towns besides those.
Give the Levites forty-eight towns in all, with their pasturelands.
Take the towns from the Israelites’ own land. Take more from larger groups and fewer from smaller ones. Each group will give the Levites towns in proportion to the inheritance it receives.”
Yahweh told Moses:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
pick towns to serve as places of refuge. Anyone who kills a person by accident can run there.
Those towns will protect the person from the avenger, so the person who caused the death won’t die before standing trial in front of the community.
Set aside six towns of refuge.
Put three across the Jordan and three in Canaan. Those will be towns of refuge.
All six will offer refuge to Israelites, to outsiders, and to foreigners living among you. Anyone who kills someone by accident can escape there.
“‘If someone strikes another person with an iron object and that person dies, it’s murder. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone strikes another person with a stone big enough to kill, and that person dies, it’s murder. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone strikes another person with a wooden weapon that can kill, and that person dies, it’s murder. The murderer must be put to death.
The avenger of blood will put the murderer to death. When the avenger meets the murderer, the avenger will kill them.
If someone shoves another person out of hatred, or lies in wait and throws something at them, and they die,
or hits them with their hand out of hostility and kills them, the person who struck them must be put to death. It’s murder. The avenger of blood will kill the murderer when they meet.
“‘But suppose someone shoves a person suddenly without hostility or throws something at them without lying in wait.
Or suppose they drop a stone big enough to kill without seeing the person below, and that person dies. They weren’t enemies and the one who dropped it wasn’t trying to hurt anyone.
In that case the community will judge between the person who caused the death and the avenger of blood, using these rules.

The community will protect the person who caused the death from the avenger of blood and send them back to the town of refuge they ran to. They must live there until the high priest, who was anointed with holy oil, dies.
“‘But if the person ever goes beyond the boundaries of the town they fled to for refuge,
and the avenger of blood finds and kills them outside those boundaries, the avenger won’t be guilty of shedding blood.
The person should have stayed in their town of refuge until the high priest died. Once the high priest dies, they can go back to their own land.
“‘These rules will stand for every generation, wherever you live.
“‘When someone kills a person, the murderer may be put to death on the testimony of witnesses. Nobody can be put to death on the word of just one witness.
“‘Don’t accept payment to spare the life of a murderer who deserves death. The murderer must be put to death.
“‘Don’t accept payment to let someone who fled to a town of refuge go back home before the priest dies.
“‘Don’t pollute the land where you live. Bloodshed pollutes the land, and the land can’t be atoned for the blood shed on it except by the blood of the one who shed it.
Don’t make the land where you live unclean. I live there too, because I, Yahweh, live among the Israelites.’”

The ancestral family heads of Gilead’s descendants came forward. Gilead was the son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from Joseph’s clans. They spoke before Moses and the leaders of Israel’s ancestral families.
They said, “Yahweh told you, my lord, to give the Israelites their land by drawing lots. Yahweh also told you to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.
If they marry into another Israelite tribe, their land will be taken out of our ancestral inheritance and added to the land of the tribe they marry into. Our share will shrink.
When Israel’s Year of Jubilee comes, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe they married into. Their land will be lost from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”
Following Yahweh’s word, Moses told the Israelites, “The tribe of Joseph’s descendants is right about this.
Here’s what Yahweh commands about Zelophehad’s daughters: ‘They can marry whoever they think best, as long as they marry within their father’s tribal clan.
That way none of Israel’s land will pass from one tribe to another. Each Israelite will keep the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.
Any daughter who inherits land in an Israelite tribe must marry someone from her father’s tribal clan, so each Israelite can keep their ancestral inheritance.
No inheritance will move from one tribe to another. Each Israelite tribe will keep its own inheritance.’”
Zelophehad’s daughters did what Yahweh had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married their father’s brothers’ sons.
They married into the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance stayed in their father’s tribal clan.
These are the commands and rulings Yahweh gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
